pathway.title: Rithm Capital Corp. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, the maturity profile is the central risk. Contractual debt at September 30, 2026 was USD 37,877.221 million on the maturity-table basis, of which USD 19,680.259 million is recourse and USD 18,196.962 million non-recourse [CP-1, chart data and calculations]. Maturities of USD 7,546.015 million in the fourth quarter of 2026 and USD 10,619.584 million in 2027 together are USD 18,165.599 million, a 15-month window holding 47.96% of the total, and USD 12,967.028 million of that window is recourse [CP-1, calculations 4]. Mechanically, most of these are secured warehouse, repurchase and servicing lines that Rithm rolls routinely, so default risk turns on lender willingness and collateral values rather than on cash generation. The implication for creditors is that a pause in secured funding markets or a fall in collateral values would force asset sales or margin posting into a thin cash cushion.

Second, liquidity is thinner than the capacity figure suggests. Unrestricted cash was USD 1,708.750 million at September 30, 2026, against USD 1,847.626 million at December 31, 2025, and 27.43% of the USD 6,230.073 million recourse maturity of the fourth quarter of 2026 [CP-1, liquidity and calculations]. Available financing of USD 10,785.284 million is stated to be uncommitted and collateral-dependent, so none of it is counted as undrawn committed liquidity. Management expects cash, operating cash flow and the ability to extend or refinance secured lines to cover needs for twelve months, and says its ability to extend or refinance short-term borrowings is critical to its outlook [CP-1, liquidity]. The implication is that headroom cannot be measured from the pack, and margin calls on USD 14.2 billion of secured financing agreements would draw on the same cash.

Third, leverage is high on a total basis and lower on a recourse basis. Principal-basis debt to equity in Rithm Capital Corp. was 4.39x at September 30, 2026 against 4.20x at December 31, 2025, and recourse debt to equity was 2.28x against 2.31x [CP-1, calculations 6]. Neither is a covenant measure and recourse debt includes collateralised repurchase and warehouse borrowings. No EBITDA is reported, so conventional leverage and cover ratios are not supplied.

Fourth, earnings quality is weak relative to the funding stack. Pre-tax income plus interest expense over interest expense was 1.54x for nine months 2026, 1.48x for nine months 2025 and 1.49x for FY2025, and includes fair value changes on mortgage servicing rights; the change in fair value of MSRs net of hedges was a gain in Q3 2026 and a loss in nine months 2026 [CP-1, calculations 7; CP-1, base view]. Net income for nine months 2026 was USD 438.665 million against USD 627.514 million, income tax expense was USD 321.554 million against a benefit of USD 27.456 million while cash taxes were USD 11.398 million, so the tax charge appears to be largely non-cash, Analyst Interpretation [CP-1, financials table]. Origination and Servicing produced USD 968.563 million of segment pre-tax income in nine months 2026, against group pre-tax income of USD 760.219 million, so the other segments and corporate costs net to a loss [CP-1A, company and operating model]. Asset Management reported a pre-tax loss of USD 83.484 million and Commercial Real Estate a loss of USD 74.855 million.

Fifth, the notes sit behind other claims. The three senior unsecured notes, USD 775.000 million at 8.000% due 2029, USD 500.000 million at 8.000% due 2030 and USD 500.000 million at 8.500% due 2031, are unsecured, were not guaranteed by any subsidiary at issuance, and require Total Unencumbered Assets of at least 120% of unsecured debt [CP-1, debt instruments; CP-1A, transaction summary]. Collateral of consolidated securitization entities is not available to other creditors of the parent. Total Unencumbered Assets is not printed, so headroom on the 120% test cannot be calculated. As a recovery mechanic only, residual value for noteholders is what remains after secured and subsidiary creditors, and no recovery outcome is concluded here.

Sixth, governance on documented actions is neutral. No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, the REIT distribution rule requires regular payouts, a Series F preferred was issued in January 2026, and no priming, uptiering or collateral release is documented, but legal capacity under the indentures cannot be assessed because they were not supplied [CP-1A, governance table].

runs.text: Strengths. Scale and diversification: nine-month 2026 revenue of USD 4,423.413 million came from five segments, with Origination and Servicing the largest by assets, equity and earnings, and the servicing portfolio of about USD 878.9 billion of unpaid principal balance is a recurring-fee base [CP-1A, company profile; Documentary Fact]. Demonstrated market access: the 8.500% notes due 2031 were issued on May 14, 2026 for net proceeds of about USD 493.7 million, a Series F preferred raised about USD 242.1 million in January 2026, and management reports several securitizations in Q3 2026, which is Management Language [CP-1A, transaction summary]. Stated compliance: the filings say Rithm was in compliance with all debt covenants and that about USD 1.1 billion of liquidity at the servicers exceeds regulatory requirements, Documentary Fact but unverifiable without the agreements [CP-1, liquidity and covenants]. Lower recourse leverage than total leverage: recourse debt to equity of 2.28x is about half the total ratio of 4.39x, Analyst Interpretation of the CP-1 ratios. Transparency: quarterly reporting, an unqualified FY2025 audit and effective disclosure controls support monitoring, Documentary Fact [CP-1A, governance table].

Weaknesses. Refinancing concentration: USD 18,165.599 million of debt falls due within the 15 months to December 31, 2027, Documentary Fact and derived [CP-1]. Uncommitted funding: available financing is uncommitted and collateral-dependent, Documentary Fact. Earnings sensitivity and negative operating cash flow: operating cash flow for nine months 2026 was an outflow of USD 1,313.851 million because loans originated for sale are in operating cash flow, offset by financing inflows of USD 3,597.283 million; this is Documentary Fact and the reading that the group depends on continuous external funding is Analyst Interpretation [CP-1, financials table]. Structural subordination of the unsecured notes, Analyst Interpretation of the guarantee and recourse facts. Loss-making new segments after the December 2025 acquisitions of Crestline and Paramount (now Elecor), whose depreciation and amortization of USD 278.619 million for nine months 2026 compares with USD 71.492 million a year earlier, Documentary Fact [CP-1A, company and operating model]. Unmeasured items: ratings, covenant levels and committed liquidity are Insufficient Information, and their absence is not an adverse conclusion.

Thesis. The credit rests on a profitable servicing and origination core and demonstrated access to secured and unsecured funding, set against a large, short-dated and partly uncommitted funding stack that leaves the senior unsecured noteholders exposed to refinancing and structural subordination.

runs.text: There is no sponsor transaction, buyout or recapitalisation in the pack; the context lists no deal terms. The transactions below are the issuer's own financings and acquisitions, with status and liquidity effect.

On May 14, 2026 Rithm Capital Corp. issued US$500.0 million of 8.500% senior unsecured notes due June 1, 2031 in a private offering, for net proceeds of approximately US$493.7 million, under an indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association; interest is payable on June 1 and December 1 from December 1, 2026; the notes are redeemable from June 1, 2028 at 104.250 stepping to 100.000 from 2030, and before then at a make-whole price or up to 40% at 108.500 with equity proceeds; they rank equally with the Company's other senior unsecured debt and were not guaranteed by any subsidiary at issuance (10-Q Q3 page:58 to page:59). The 10-Q does not state the use of proceeds in the text read; the nine-month cash flow statement shows repayment of unsecured notes of US$18,326 thousand and no large unsecured repayment, so the issue increased unsecured debt (10-Q Q3 page:13). Status: closed and outstanding. Liquidity effect: adds to cash and extends the unsecured profile to 2031; it also adds interest cost at 8.500%. Earlier senior notes: US$500.0 million of 8.000% notes due July 15, 2030 issued June 20, 2025, and US$775.0 million of 8.000% notes due April 1, 2029 issued March 19, 2024 (10-Q Q3 page:168); the notes due October 15, 2025 were redeemed in the second quarter of 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:63). The three outstanding notes each carry a requirement that Total Unencumbered Assets be not less than 120% of outstanding unsecured debt, and the 2029 and 2030 notes carry a 101% repurchase right on a change of control or Mortgage Business Triggering Event (10-Q Q3 page:61; page:63; page:168).

On January 13, 2026 Rithm priced 10,000,000 shares of 8.750% Series F Fixed-Rate Reset Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock with a US$25.00 liquidation preference for net proceeds of approximately US$242.1 million (10-Q Q3 page:111). This is equity-like capital that ranks below the notes in the capital structure as presented; it adds a fixed cash dividend obligation, but it is not debt. The Series D dividend rate resets on November 15, 2026 to the five-year Treasury rate plus 6.223% (10-Q Q3 page:174); this is a future-dated term, not a fact about Q3 2026.

On December 1, 2025 Rithm completed the acquisition of Crestline for cash consideration of US$324.7 million, recognising goodwill of approximately US$182.8 million; it brought insurance company investments at fair value of US$844,822 thousand and interest sensitive insurance contract liabilities of US$920,776 thousand (10-Q Q3 page:20). On December 19, 2025 it completed the acquisition of Paramount Group, now Elecor, for total consideration of approximately US$1.8 billion, accounted for as an asset acquisition with no goodwill (10-Q Q3 page:20). The 10-K cash flow statement shows "Acquisition of Paramount, net of cash acquired" of US$903,606 thousand and non-cash "Assumed financing in Paramount transaction" of US$3,706,617 thousand (10-K page:232 to page:233); the mix of cash, equity and assumed debt inside the US$1.8 billion consideration is not stated in the text read, so that composition is Insufficient Information and the two cash-flow figures are not reconciled to it here. Liquidity effect: the cash outlay and the assumed property debt weigh on balance sheet leverage (CP-1) and the acquisitions explain the step-up in depreciation and amortization and the first commercial real estate revenue.

During Q3 2026 Elecor sold a 49% interest in a CRE joint venture to an unrelated third party, deconsolidated it and recognised a gain of US$26.8 million; the Note 17 roll-forward shows US$900,000 thousand of secured notes on real estate deconsolidated in the nine months (10-Q Q3 page:38; page:56). The release says management closed a joint venture for ownership of 1301 Avenue of the Americas and a US$515 million refinancing of 31 West 52nd Street (release Q3 page:2); that is Management Language, and which transaction produced the deconsolidated debt is an inference not stated in the filing. Other Q3 2026 financing items attributed to management: an inaugural US$375 million securitization of multifamily RTLs, two NQM securitizations totalling US$975 million of UPB and a US$306 million securitization of home improvement loans (release Q3 page:2). The Upgrade forward flow agreement was amended to extend expiry from October 31, 2026 to August 21, 2027 and to add US$1.2 billion of UPB of purchase commitments (10-Q Q3 page:35). A purchase of Agency RMBS of US$535,039 thousand was settled after quarter-end (10-Q Q3 page:13); this is a subsequent settlement, not a Q3 2026 balance. The Q3 10-Q is signed October 30, 2026 and reports no subsequent events requiring disclosure (10-Q Q3 page:125; page:186). Nothing dated after the cutoff is used as fact.

fields.value: The financial base is usable but must be read as a specialty-finance balance sheet rather than an operating-company credit. The group funds a mortgage, servicing, transitional-lending, asset-management and commercial real estate book mainly with secured repurchase and warehouse lines, secured notes and bonds, and consolidated securitization and fund debt, with a small layer of parent senior unsecured notes. Total contractual debt at September 30, 2026 was US$37,877.221m on the maturity-table basis, of which US$19,680.259m is classed as recourse and US$18,196.962m as non-recourse (10-Q Q3 page:57). The filings report no EBITDA, so the leverage and cover charts carry "Not supplied" and the credit read rests on debt to equity, the recourse split, the maturity profile, unrestricted cash and earnings cover of interest, all derived in Calculations. The strongest contrary evidence to a benign view is the maturity wall: US$7,546.015m falls due October 1 to December 31, 2026 and US$10,619.584m in 2027, and available financing is stated to be uncommitted. Earnings are market-sensitive: the change in fair value of MSRs net of economic hedges was a gain of 121,277 in Q3 2026 against a loss of 264,351 in Q3 2025, and a loss of 475,827 in nine months 2026 against a loss of 752,734 in nine months 2025 (US$ thousands, 10-Q Q3 page:8), and nine-month 2026 net income of 438,665 is below 627,514 in nine months 2025. Earnings available for distribution, a non-GAAP measure, were US$315.3m in Q3 2026 against US$338.9m in Q2 2026 (release Q3 page:1). The senior unsecured notes are unsecured and, at issuance, not guaranteed by any subsidiary, so they rank behind secured lenders on pledged collateral and behind subsidiary-level debt in the structure (10-Q Q3 page:59). The strongest supportive evidence is the filed statement that Rithm was in compliance with all debt covenants at September 30, 2026 and that about US$1.1 billion of liquidity held in the servicers exceeds regulatory requirements. Neither can be tested further without the facility agreements and indentures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rithm Capital Corp. is a publicly listed, internally managed REIT that describes itself as a global asset manager focused on real estate, credit and financial services (10-K page:8). It is not a sponsor-owned credit; the pack names no controlling shareholder and the Part III ownership information is incorporated by reference from a proxy statement that is not in the pack (10-K page:3). The operating model is an integrated platform of five reported segments: Origination and Servicing (Newrez and NRM), Residential Transitional Lending (Genesis), Asset Management (Sculptor, Crestline and Rithm Advisers), Investment Portfolio and Commercial Real Estate (Elecor) (10-Q Q3 page:14 to page:16). Origination and Servicing is the largest business by assets, equity and earnings contribution (10-Q Q3 page:132); in the nine months to September 30, 2026 it produced US$968,563 thousand of segment pre-tax income against group pre-tax income of US$760,219 thousand, so the other segments and the corporate category net to a loss (10-Q Q3 page:25). The credit mechanic is that revenue in the largest segment depends on the fair value of mortgage servicing rights and on origination margins, both rate-sensitive, while funding is mostly secured and short-dated (CP-1). The December 2025 acquisitions of Crestline (cash consideration US$324.7 million, bringing insurance and reinsurance strategies and interest-sensitive insurance contract liabilities) and Paramount, now Elecor (total consideration approximately US$1.8 billion, 12.2 million square feet of Class A offices in New York City and San Francisco) are the main credit-relevant change in history (10-Q Q3 page:20; page:150). They bring fixed operating costs, depreciation and property debt: depreciation and amortization rose to US$278,619 thousand in nine months 2026 from US$71,492 thousand (10-Q Q3 page:8). Asset Management and Commercial Real Estate both reported pre-tax losses in the nine months (10-Q Q3 page:25). No leveraged buyout, sponsor recapitalisation, priming, uptiering or collateral release is documented in the pack. The financing actions documented are plain senior unsecured note issues, a preferred equity issue and securitizations, set out in the transaction summary below. What cannot be assessed is legal capacity under the notes, because the indentures are not supplied.

The 10-Q does not state the use of proceeds in the text read; the nine-month cash flow statement shows repayment of unsecured notes of US$18,326 thousand and no large unsecured repayment, so the issue increased unsecured debt (10-Q Q3 page:13). Status: closed and outstanding. Liquidity effect: adds to cash and extends the unsecured profile to 2031; it also adds interest cost at 8.500%. Earlier senior notes: US$500.0 million of 8.000% notes due July 15, 2030 issued June 20, 2025, and US$775.0 million of 8.000% notes due April 1, 2029 issued March 19, 2024 (10-Q Q3 page:168); the notes due October 15, 2025 were redeemed in the second quarter of 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:63). The three outstanding notes each carry a requirement that Total Unencumbered Assets be not less than 120% of outstanding unsecured debt, and the 2029 and 2030 notes carry a 101% repurchase right on a change of control or Mortgage Business Triggering Event (10-Q Q3 page:61; page:63; page:168).

The Upgrade forward flow agreement was amended to extend expiry from October 31, 2026 to August 21, 2027 and to add US$1.2 billion of UPB of purchase commitments (10-Q Q3 page:35). A purchase of Agency RMBS of US$535,039 thousand was settled after quarter-end (10-Q Q3 page:13); this is a subsequent settlement, not a Q3 2026 balance. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Origination and Servicing earned the large majority of nine-month 2026 segment pre-tax income, and change in fair value of MSRs net of economic hedges was a gain in Q3 2026 and a loss in nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:8; page:25). Mechanic: servicing and origination revenue depends on interest rate and prepayment moves and origination volume, so reported income can swing without a change in cash earnings. Implication: coverage of funding costs is less predictable than for a fee-based or contract-based issuer; committee should look at cash servicing fees separately from fair value changes. A logged conflict that counters this: none. A limitation that counters it: the nine months include acquisition effects.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Business mix shift. Evidence: Asset Management and Commercial Real Estate reported pre-tax losses in nine months 2026 while depreciation and amortization rose (10-Q Q3 page:8; page:25). Mechanic: acquired real estate and an asset manager add fixed costs, interest expense on property debt and depreciation before fee or rent growth scales. Implication: near-term earnings support for debt service from the new businesses is unproven; progress depends on leasing (occupancy 83.5% against 85.3% at December 31, 2025, recalculated for the joint venture sale, 10-Q Q3 page:150) and AUM inflows (management language, release Q3 page:1 to page:2).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rithm Capital Corp. is a large, diversified mortgage and real estate finance platform whose credit quality rests on refinancing short-dated, mostly secured funding rather than on stable cash earnings, and the fundamental view is neutral to cautious with medium confidence. The strongest support is a dominant, profitable Origination and Servicing segment, a stated position of compliance with all debt covenants, USD 1,708.750 million of unrestricted cash and repeated senior unsecured note issuance in 2024, 2025 and 2026. The weakest point is the maturity profile: USD 7,546.015 million falls due in Q4 2026 and USD 10,619.584 million in 2027, about half of contractual debt is recourse, and available financing is described as uncommitted. Continued access to secured funding, stable servicing values and the new real estate and asset management businesses reaching profit will decide the outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, the maturity profile is the central risk. Contractual debt at September 30, 2026 was USD 37,877.221 million on the maturity-table basis, of which USD 19,680.259 million is recourse and USD 18,196.962 million non-recourse [CP-1, chart data and calculations]. Maturities of USD 7,546.015 million in the fourth quarter of 2026 and USD 10,619.584 million in 2027 together are USD 18,165.599 million, a 15-month window holding 47.96% of the total, and USD 12,967.028 million of that window is recourse [CP-1, calculations 4]. Mechanically, most of these are secured warehouse, repurchase and servicing lines that Rithm rolls routinely, so default risk turns on lender willingness and collateral values rather than on cash generation. The implication for creditors is that a pause in secured funding markets or a fall in collateral values would force asset sales or margin posting into a thin cash cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, liquidity is thinner than the capacity figure suggests. Unrestricted cash was USD 1,708.750 million at September 30, 2026, against USD 1,847.626 million at December 31, 2025, and 27.43% of the USD 6,230.073 million recourse maturity of the fourth quarter of 2026 [CP-1, liquidity and calculations]. Available financing of USD 10,785.284 million is stated to be uncommitted and collateral-dependent, so none of it is counted as undrawn committed liquidity. Management expects cash, operating cash flow and the ability to extend or refinance secured lines to cover needs for twelve months, and says its ability to extend or refinance short-term borrowings is critical to its outlook [CP-1, liquidity]. The implication is that headroom cannot be measured from the pack, and margin calls on USD 14.2 billion of secured financing agreements would draw on the same cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, leverage is high on a total basis and lower on a recourse basis. Principal-basis debt to equity in Rithm Capital Corp. was 4.39x at September 30, 2026 against 4.20x at December 31, 2025, and recourse debt to equity was 2.28x against 2.31x [CP-1, calculations 6]. Neither is a covenant measure and recourse debt includes collateralised repurchase and warehouse borrowings. No EBITDA is reported, so conventional leverage and cover ratios are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, earnings quality is weak relative to the funding stack. Pre-tax income plus interest expense over interest expense was 1.54x for nine months 2026, 1.48x for nine months 2025 and 1.49x for FY2025, and includes fair value changes on mortgage servicing rights; the change in fair value of MSRs net of hedges was a gain in Q3 2026 and a loss in nine months 2026 [CP-1, calculations 7; CP-1, base view]. Net income for nine months 2026 was USD 438.665 million against USD 627.514 million, income tax expense was USD 321.554 million against a benefit of USD 27.456 million while cash taxes were USD 11.398 million, so the tax charge appears to be largely non-cash, Analyst Interpretation [CP-1, financials table]. Origination and Servicing produced USD 968.563 million of segment pre-tax income in nine months 2026, against group pre-tax income of USD 760.219 million, so the other segments and corporate costs net to a loss [CP-1A, company and operating model]. Asset Management reported a pre-tax loss of USD 83.484 million and Commercial Real Estate a loss of USD 74.855 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, the notes sit behind other claims. The three senior unsecured notes, USD 775.000 million at 8.000% due 2029, USD 500.000 million at 8.000% due 2030 and USD 500.000 million at 8.500% due 2031, are unsecured, were not guaranteed by any subsidiary at issuance, and require Total Unencumbered Assets of at least 120% of unsecured debt [CP-1, debt instruments; CP-1A, transaction summary]. Collateral of consolidated securitization entities is not available to other creditors of the parent. Total Unencumbered Assets is not printed, so headroom on the 120% test cannot be calculated. As a recovery mechanic only, residual value for noteholders is what remains after secured and subsidiary creditors, and no recovery outcome is concluded here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, governance on documented actions is neutral. No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, the REIT distribution rule requires regular payouts, a Series F preferred was issued in January 2026, and no priming, uptiering or collateral release is documented, but legal capacity under the indentures cannot be assessed because they were not supplied [CP-1A, governance table].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Scale and diversification: nine-month 2026 revenue of USD 4,423.413 million came from five segments, with Origination and Servicing the largest by assets, equity and earnings, and the servicing portfolio of about USD 878.9 billion of unpaid principal balance is a recurring-fee base [CP-1A, company profile; Documentary Fact]. Demonstrated market access: the 8.500% notes due 2031 were issued on May 14, 2026 for net proceeds of about USD 493.7 million, a Series F preferred raised about USD 242.1 million in January 2026, and management reports several securitizations in Q3 2026, which is Management Language [CP-1A, transaction summary]. Stated compliance: the filings say Rithm was in compliance with all debt covenants and that about USD 1.1 billion of liquidity at the servicers exceeds regulatory requirements, Documentary Fact but unverifiable without the agreements [CP-1, liquidity and covenants]. Lower recourse leverage than total leverage: recourse debt to equity of 2.28x is about half the total ratio of 4.39x, Analyst Interpretation of the CP-1 ratios. Transparency: quarterly reporting, an unqualified FY2025 audit and effective disclosure controls support monitoring, Documentary Fact [CP-1A, governance table].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Refinancing concentration: USD 18,165.599 million of debt falls due within the 15 months to December 31, 2027, Documentary Fact and derived [CP-1]. Uncommitted funding: available financing is uncommitted and collateral-dependent, Documentary Fact. Earnings sensitivity and negative operating cash flow: operating cash flow for nine months 2026 was an outflow of USD 1,313.851 million because loans originated for sale are in operating cash flow, offset by financing inflows of USD 3,597.283 million; this is Documentary Fact and the reading that the group depends on continuous external funding is Analyst Interpretation [CP-1, financials table]. Structural subordination of the unsecured notes, Analyst Interpretation of the guarantee and recourse facts. Loss-making new segments after the December 2025 acquisitions of Crestline and Paramount (now Elecor), whose depreciation and amortization of USD 278.619 million for nine months 2026 compares with USD 71.492 million a year earlier, Documentary Fact [CP-1A, company and operating model]. Unmeasured items: ratings, covenant levels and committed liquidity are Insufficient Information, and their absence is not an adverse conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thesis. The credit rests on a profitable servicing and origination core and demonstrated access to secured and unsecured funding, set against a large, short-dated and partly uncommitted funding stack that leaves the senior unsecured noteholders exposed to refinancing and structural subordination.
